heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles eSUN PETG exceptionally well out of the box with its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame design. Running at an effective volumetric flow cap of 14 mm³/s, the machine achieves reliable, defect-free prints up to a calculated safe speed of 167 mm/s.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (Wipe clean with Isopropyl Alcohol; use glue stick as a release agent if printing on smooth PEI to avoid tear-out)
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap print speeds safely near 167 mm/s.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (set to 2 mm) and select 'Retract on layer change' to minimize PETG nozzle oozing and stringing.
Configure Part Cooling Fan thresholds: 20% minimum fan speed, 50% maximum fan speed, and set 'Keep fan always on' to maintain layer bond strength without curling.
Adjust Pressure Advance (Linear Advance) to approximately 0.038 s to sharpen corners and prevent material bulges.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine filament webbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and absorbed ambient moisture, lowering melt viscosity, or retraction/travel settings are not aggressive enough.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, increase travel speed to 400 mm/s, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive bed adhesion tearing PEI coating upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds molecularly to smooth PEI surfaces under high bed temperatures.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to the Bambu Textured PEI plate or apply a thin, uniform layer of PVP glue stick / liquid release agent on smooth surfaces, and allow the plate to cool below 35°C before removing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle layer bonding or parts delaminating along layer lines
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extruded PETG bead too quickly, preventing adequate molecular cross-linking.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce cooling fan speed to 20-30% nominal, limit maximum fan speed to 50%, and raise nozzle temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN PETG on the P1P without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Yes. PETG does not require a heated chamber and prints best in open-frame environments like the P1P because excessive ambient heat can cause heat creep or reduce cooling efficiency.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: No. Standard eSUN PETG is non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel nozzle on the P1P completely safe to use without accelerated wear.

faq.question: Why is my maximum print speed capped at 167 mm/s?
faq.answer: Given eSUN PETG's melt behavior, the reliable volumetric flow limit is 14 mm³/s. With standard 0.4 mm line widths and 0.2 mm layer heights, 167 mm/s represents the theoretical volumetric ceiling before underextrusion occurs.

faq.question: What is the recommended drying procedure for eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: Dry the filament in a dedicated filament dryer or convection oven at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours. Store below 20% relative humidity to avoid popping, stringing, and degraded mechanical properties.
